issues.title: These elements with an explicit role of listitem are not children in the accessibility tree of an element with their required context role, but of an element with the tabpanel role.
issues.why_it_matters_for_persona: As an autistic person, I depend on a logical and predictable structure to understand web content. When list items are nested inside another element that isn't their list container, the semantic relationship is broken. My screen reader may not announce the list correctly, or announce the items without the context that they belong to a list. This inconsistency is confusing and increases the cognitive effort required to understand the page layout.
remediation_instructions: Ensure that any element with `role="listitem"` is a direct child of its container with `role="list"`.
Remove the intermediate `<div role="tabpanel">` from between the list and listitem elements.

The corrected structure should be: `
...
...
`.
expected_tool_change: An automated accessibility checker will no longer report an error about a missing required parent for the list items.
A screen reader will correctly announce the beginning of the list, the number of items, and each list item within that context.
